classifiedFinding.title: claim() / stake() / withdraw() violate CEI; cross-function reentrancy lever conditional on hooked-token semantics

classification.assetImpact: Conditional on rewardToken having ERC777-style callbacks OR phUSD.mint dispatching to user-controlled code: double-claim of pending rewards and (for withdraw) totalStaked corruption. Under documented trust assumptions, none of these tokens have callbacks.
attackPath: 1. Governance points rewardToken at a hooked ERC20 (e.g., ERC777). [NOT TRUE under current trust model]
2. Attacker stakes and accumulates pending rewards.
3. Attacker calls claim(); _claimRewards triggers rewardToken.safeTransfer → hook re-enters claim().
4. Inner claim() reads pre-rebase debts → re-pays same pending amount.
classification.likelihood: low — exploit is gated on token-callback semantics that profile §10 explicitly excludes from trust assumptions
classification.assumptions: Either phUSD or rewardToken is a hooked / callback-capable ERC20

classifiedFinding.justification: Profile §10 trust assumptions explicitly exclude callback-capable tokens (phUSD non-callback; rewardToken non-hooked vanilla ERC20). Per C4 known-invalid rules, 'Non-standard / weird ERC-20 tokens' are not valid scope. The defect is a real defense-in-depth gap (missing nonReentrant), but exploit requires violating documented trust assumptions. Classified as Low/QA — recommend adding nonReentrant as cheap belt-and-braces.
classifiedFinding.notes: Sanitizer hinted potential-high. Classifier downgrades to Low because exploit is conditional on a token category the protocol explicitly excludes. Surfacing as QA defense-in-depth recommendation.
